name: Bharati Nayak

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Bharati Nayak writes poetry in Odia and English and also works in translation. Her collections include Padma Paada in Odia and Words Are Such Perfect Traitors and A Day for Myself in English. Her collaborative work includes In the Realms of Love & Divinity with Antony Theodore, and she edited the third volume of Radical Rhythm. Quilled Ink Press also documents her Odia translation project with Adiela Akoo’s Lost in a Quatrain.

In “A Day For Myself,” the speaker asks to keep one day from a life generously given away. Flowers, butterfly colours, a cuckoo’s song, rain, sky and sea become gifts with which to renew the self and its poetry. On her author page, Nayak identifies this English poem as her translation of her own Odia poem “Nija Paain Dinatie,” making it a small meeting place between her two writing languages.
